title: Choose Tasks with when Conditions
objective: Use gathered facts to select distribution-appropriate tasks without hiding failures.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 07 - The 'when' Conditional
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A when expression decides whether a task applies to the current host. Common gates compare gathered facts such as ansible_distribution or inspect a previously registered result.
A skipped task is not a failure; it means its condition evaluated false. This allows one play to express alternatives for different operating-system families while keeping each module call explicit.
Quote values, not the entire Jinja expression. Prefer a small number of readable conditions over a dense expression that obscures why a host receives a task.
explanation.rule: Use facts to select valid desired state; do not use conditions merely to silence errors.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
- name: Install a web server on Debian-family hosts
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: nginx
    state: present
  when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

feedback.correct: Correct—this matches the demonstrated workflow and keeps the automation explicit.
feedback.incorrect: Review the rule of thumb and the relevant video checkpoint before continuing.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Use gathered facts to select distribution-appropriate tasks without hiding failures.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

assignment.title: Gate a Debian Task
assignment.brief: Write a package task that runs only for the Debian OS family.
requirements: Include every named safety or behavior requirement.
assignment.solutionCode:
- name: Install a Debian package
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: nginx
    state: present
  when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
assignment.outputCheckLabel: Artifact uses valid course-style YAML structure

lab.title: Run a fact-driven play
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Save the conditional task inside a webservers play.
Run ansible-playbook --check and note which hosts match.
Change Debian to RedHat and observe skipped results without applying changes.
lab.success: Facts report Debian and explain which form of the conditional runs.
